fields.title: 3. Picking up the unpublished 11/18 and 11/19 runs — what was re-checked against the originals
fields.md:
A copy is not a source. This section lists only what this run re-opened and confirmed against the original text (source: `_probe/unpublished/` · `state.run.unpublished_runs`).

### 3-1. $40 billion GPU financing — the lessor-side bonds (T5)

| Item | Bloomberg (11/17 09:53 EST) | Semafor (11/18 07:53 EST) |
|---|---|---|
| Reporters | Carpenter·Arroyo·Smith | Ellen DiMauro (exclusive) |
| Structure | An SPV run by Atlas SP, an Apollo affiliate, buys Nvidia chips and issues ABS | SPV, 7 tranches |
| Size | 'Part' of the $40 billion — size of the part not given | Total $40 billion · Apollo pre-funds about $20 billion, then sells down |
| Interest rate | None | $35.5 billion at 8.3% and 7.75% · the risk tranche (under $3 billion in total) could exceed a blended 9% |
| Timing | 'as soon as this week' | 'as early as this week' |
| Accounting wording | 'designed to keep the debt off SpaceX's balance sheet' · investment grade maintained | Off its own books |
| Source | 1 anonymous source · no SpaceX comment | Apollo declined to comment · SpaceX did not respond |

(Sources: ⑤ [Bloomberg (Yahoo-published version)](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/spacex-debt-ai-chips-hit-145310043.html) · ⑥ [Semafor](https://www.semafor.com/article/11/18/2026/spacex-40-billion-chip-financing-to-stay-off-balance-sheet))

- **Layer breakdown**: The 10/26 8-K is a master finance lease commitment between the lessee (SpaceX) and the lessor. Principal is about $40 billion, and the fixed rate is set at pricing before signing. The reported SPV·ABS is how the lessor raises the money to buy the chips, so it sits at a different layer and does not contradict the 8-K (source: ① [8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000110465926118614/tm2628247d1_8k.htm), 2026-10-26).
- **Interest rate**: The SPV bond rate is the lessor's funding cost. Judging from the 8-K's rent structure (tranche financing cost 1/20 + fixed-rate interest), it could be close to the lease fixed rate. But no source text says they are the same. So it is not an input to proposed new rule ② (source: 8-K, 2026-10-26 · `state.rule_proposals_not_applied`).
- **'Off-balance-sheet' wording**: That the SPV bonds are not SpaceX's debt is a separate matter from whether SpaceX recognizes a lease liability. The determination is made in the first 10-Q after lease commencement (proposal ③) (source: `state.rule_proposals_not_applied`).
- **Judgment layer**: Since it is the same $40 billion, the input to D-2027-1 (additional financing of $50 billion or less AND no equity raise) is unchanged. SPV bonds are not an issuance of SpaceX equity, so R3 does not apply either (source: `state.milestones[D-2027-1]`).
- **New developments**: No report of pricing or closing was found in the 2026-11-20 KST search. There is also no 8-K for signing (source: [EDGAR submissions](https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001181412.json), 2026-11-20 KST).
- **Not adopted**: The expected ratings (Moody's A3 · KBRA A-), the CFO's remarks, and the 'about $4 billion bond' that a secondary summary relayed while citing Bloomberg. They are not in the published Bloomberg version, and no original text was found (source: `state.run.unpublished_runs[2026-11-19-event].not_absorbed`).

### 3-2. T7 responses by channel — ⓒ lapsed, ⓕ new

| Channel | Sender → recipient | Sent | Deadline | Status (2026-11-20 KST) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ⓐ | 9 Senators → DoD Inspector General | 10/15 | 11/01 | Declined (10/27) — referred to the Air Force | [Senate Foreign Relations Committee](https://www.foreign.senate.gov/press/dem/release/shaheen-tillis-lead-bipartisan-senators-in-calling-for-department-of-defense-inspector-general-investigation-into-starlink-disruptions-in-ukraine) |
| ⓑ | Inspector General referral → Department of the Air Force·Space Force | 10/27 | None | No response | [AP (Yahoo reprint)](https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/pentagon-watchdog-refuses-investigate-starlink-014800041.html) |
| ⓒ | House Appropriations DeLauro·McCollum → Secretary of Defense | 10/19 | 11/18 | **Deadline passed — no public reply found** | [Appropriations Committee minority press releases](https://democrats-appropriations.house.gov/news/press-releases) |
| ⓓ | Blumenthal → Secretary of Defense | 10/22 | 11/05 · 11/12 | Deadline passed — no public reply found | [Kyiv Independent](https://kyivindependent.com/us-senator-blumenthal-opens-probe-into-ukraine-starshield-restrictions/) |
| ⓔ | 3 House members → White House Chief of Staff | 10/23 | 11/06 | Deadline passed — no public reply found | [SF Standard](https://sfstandard.com/2026/10/23/liccardo-panetta-khanna-letter-white-house-starshield-ukraine/) |
| **ⓕ** | **Senate Foreign Relations Shaheen·Coons → SpaceX chairman** | **11/13** | **11/30** | **Pending (newly listed)** | [Letter, original PDF](https://www.foreign.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/11132026%20Letter%20to%20Elon%20Musk%20and%20SpaceX%20on%20Starshield%20and%20Starlink.pdf) |

- **ⓒ check**: The November entries in the Appropriations minority press releases number 4 (11/15·16·17·19), and all are unrelated to Ukraine. No response is recorded as 'not made public', not as a refusal (source: [Appropriations Committee minority press releases](https://democrats-appropriations.house.gov/news/press-releases), checked 2026-11-20 KST).
- **What the ⓕ letter requested**: It asked that all records since 2026-09-01 be preserved. There are 3 questions. ① Who conveyed, approved or directed the restrictions after 10/1 (including whether direction came from outside SpaceX) ② An impact assessment and a chronology of restrictions and restorations ③ Who approved the restrictions now maintained or resumed and the one that recurred on 11/12. Both the preservation confirmation and the answers are due by **2026-11-30**. The letter states 'To date, SpaceX has not provided any explanation or clarification of who authorized these restrictions' (source: [Letter, original PDF](https://www.foreign.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/11132026%20Letter%20to%20Elon%20Musk%20and%20SpaceX%20on%20Starshield%20and%20Starlink.pdf), 2026-11-13).
- **Forecast check — wrong**: The forecast was 'a response on 11/19 (KST) = ⓒ 11/18 + 1 day', but in fact the deadline passed with no response. There were two faulty premises. ① The deadline was read as 'the day a response comes'. A deadline is only 'the day one could come'. ② The searches in the 11/14–11/18 runs were aimed only at letters to government agencies, so the letter to SpaceX (ⓕ) was missed. **Fix**: No response is not counted as an event and is carried over to the next channel's deadline. The next checkpoint is ⓕ 11/30 + 1 day KST = **12/01** (monthly). When searching congressional channels, letters addressed to the company are included too (source: `state.triggers_next_12m[T7].prev_2026_11_20`).

### 3-3. November Starshield restrictions (T7 ③ · E-2027-3 candidate) — determination remains pending

| Date | Source | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11/17 | Ukrainian president's X post | 'The speed limit on Starshield in the temporarily occupied territories remains in place. We are discussing this with the American side.' | ⑤ [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/ukraine-starshield-starlink-musk-spacex.html), 2026-11-17 21:50 EST (Kolodny·Lim) |
| 11/17 | SpaceX | No immediate response | Same as above |
| 11/17 | Canadian Defense Minister McGuinty | Said the prime minister would raise the issue with Trump | Same as above |
| 11/12 | WSJ | 'Ukraine Says Its Military Starlink Is Disrupted Again, Hurting Defenses' — body behind paywall, existence confirmed only via letter footnote | ⑤ [Letter footnote 3](https://www.foreign.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/11132026%20Letter%20to%20Elon%20Musk%20and%20SpaceX%20on%20Starshield%20and%20Starlink.pdf) |

- **Check against the determination rule** (fixed 2026-11-16, before the results): To count as a decision, it requires ① official acknowledgment by the US government or SpaceX, or ② with the Ukrainian government announcement still standing, two top-tier reports independently confirming a 'decision or instruction'. ① is absent. The letter itself says 'there is no explanation yet'. For ②, CNBC and WSJ reported, but within the range read it cannot be told whether they relayed the government announcement or confirmed independently. Therefore **the determination remains pending**. There is also no announcement of a lifting (11/20 KST search) (source: `state.milestones[E-2027-3].progress.candidates[0].update_2026_11_20`).
- **E-2027-3**: It is already 'not met' on 1 case, and the status does not change. Proposal ④, which would give bearish +5 on the 2nd case, is not adopted, so even if confirmed it is not put into this run's numbers (source: `state.rule_proposals_not_applied`).

### 3-4. NSSL Phase 3 Lane 2 — ceiling increase (T13 ④)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Announcement date | 2026-11-16 (DoD contract announcement — the original could not be opened; checked against a reprint) |
| Subjects | SpaceX FA8811-25-D-B002 (P00006) · United Launch Services B003 (P00004) · Blue Origin B005 (P00006) |
| Increase | Combined ceiling $985 million — no per-company share |
| Performance period · obligation | Through 2033-04 · no additional obligation at time of award |
| Lead office | Space Systems Command Space Access (Los Angeles Air Force Base) |

(Source: ⑥ [The Defense Watch](https://thedefensewatch.com/cyber-space-defense/spacex-ula-blue-origin-985-million-nssl-contract/), 2026-11-16)

- **Judgment layer**: The ceiling is the upper limit on task orders that may be issued going forward, not an award. E-2027-4 is measured only by award amount. The announcement gives no reason. 'One day after the Vulcan failure' is the reports linking the timing together → **T13 ④ record only** (source: `state.milestones[E-2027-4].progress_reason`).
